newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach confirms P'brook compliance plan.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach confirms P'brook compliance plan.

text.p: Stagecoach Holdings Plc confirmed on Friday that it would comply with British regulators' conditions on its acquisition of Porterbrook Leasing Co, which was completed in August.
It added that Porterbrook expected to announce shortly a plan to order 30 new trains worth about 90 million stg for use by South West Trains, which was taken over by Stagecoach in December 1995.

Earlier, Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said it would refer the deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) unless suitable legally-binding undertakings were obtained from the international bus and train operator.
Stagecoach responded in a statement that it would accept the undertakings, which it said were broadly in line with its previous preparations, in place of referral to the MMC.

It added that Porterbrook had already demonstrated its commitment to rail network development with a new passenger train order for Chiltern Railway Co and refurbishment of over 580 of its vehicles operated by West Coast Mainline, Midland Mainline, Cross Country and Anglia.
Porterbrook's order for 30 new trains would comprise 120 vehicles to be delivered during 1998, the company said.
